line: One day in New York in time-lapse: rivers of light, a grid on the sixteenths, 1899 beside today.
line_cn: 纽约的一天：延时光河、踩着十六分音符的网格，1899 年和今天并排。

motion.cuts: camera-led cuts: slide or push-through on motion

camera.expresses: grid cells light every 1–2 frames; cells re-cut every sixteenth

camera.move: Dry cut of the whole ensemble, reverb left ringing
camera.expresses: hard cut to black on the bar line

transitions: numbers at 120 BPM and 30 fps: 1 beat = 15 frames, triplet = 5, sixteenth = 3.75) Rules: - Cuts land on beats.
All cut times come from one function, bar(n, beat) in tools/timeline.py;
The editor never cuts faster than the current subdivision, and the slowest picture sits under the place where the arpeggios stop.
labels: Latin: Michroma (OFL), capitals, tracking 0.06–0.32 em. Chinese: Noto Sans SC variable, weight 300–350, tracking 0.08–0.14 em. Credits: Noto Sans SC 17 px.
Left-aligned, left margin 168–196 px, never centred, never on a box. Legibility comes from a very soft elliptical darkening behind the block (α ≤ 0.6), not a panel.

Number card: the number in Michroma 84 px (44 px when three numbers stack); a 2 px sodium rule grows under it; one Chinese line (28 px) and one English line (14–16 px) say what it counts and the source year. A census-type number locks digit by digit on sixteenths (one glockenspiel note per digit); a flow number counts up from 0 in 0.6 s (ease-out). "About" numbers carry ≈ and "约".
Archive date: just the year, Michroma 22 px, bottom-left of the archive panel.
motion: Speed is the main instrument. Shot speeds run from 0.3× to 75×; every speed above 1× uses frame blending (a 360° shutter): each output frame averages the source frames it covers, capped at N frames. Headlights become continuous lines, crowds become fog, clouds become water.

Speed ramps are smooth (smoothstep between key speeds) and always mean something: a corridor accelerates out of real time (1× → 6×), a time-lapse ramps into a frenzy (1× → 7×), a fast shot brakes into slow motion (2.2× → 0.3× in 0.55 s) on the bar where the music stops.

Camera moves are added sparingly in post: slow push-ins (1.00 → 1.05–1.10 over the shot), a falling push on the opening still (1.0 → 1.3 in 0.35 s, ease-out, then accelerating to ×2 by the cut). No shakes, no whip pans, no digital zooms past the upscale limit.

score.note: music only: organ, staccato winds, spiccato strings, additive layering
